hints: Look at the oxidation numbers of chlorine and bromine before and after the reaction to see if electrons are transferred.
Chlorine goes from 0 in $Cl_2$ to -1 in $NaCl$, while bromine goes from -1 in $NaBr$ to 0 in $Br_2$, so one is reduced and the other is oxidised.
Remember disproportionation needs the same element to be both oxidised and reduced, then check if that happens here and if a more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one.
walkthrough:
**Assign oxidation numbers**

Start by tracking what happens to each halogen. This tells you if it is redox.

$$Cl \text{ in } Cl_2 = 0 \to Cl \text{ in } NaCl = -1$$
$$Br \text{ in } NaBr = -1 \to Br \text{ in } Br_2 = 0$$

**Decide if it is redox**

Chlorine gains an electron, so it is reduced. Bromine loses an electron, so it is oxidised.

$$\frac{1}{2}Cl_2 + e^- \to Cl^- \text{ (reduction)}$$
$$Br^- \to \frac{1}{2}Br_2 + e^- \text{ (oxidation)}$$ 
Since both oxidation and reduction occur, statement 1 is correct.

**Decide if it is displacement**

A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halogen from its salt. Chlorine is above bromine in Group 17, so chlorine pushes bromine out of sodium bromide to form sodium chloride. So statement 2 is correct.

**Decide if it is disproportionation**

Disproportionation is special. The same element must be both oxidised and reduced in the same reaction.
Here chlorine is only reduced and bromine is only oxidised. They are different elements, so statement 3 is incorrect.
Therefore 1 and 2 only is correct.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes 3. This is not disproportionation since two different elements change: Cl is only reduced and Br is only oxidised. Disproportionation requires one element to do both.
options.B: Correct. It is redox because $Cl$ (0 to -1) is reduced and $Br$ (-1 to 0) is oxidised. It is displacement because the more reactive chlorine displaces bromine from NaBr.
options.C: Incorrect because it leaves out 2. While it is redox, it is also clearly a halogen displacement reaction where $Cl_2$ displaces $Br_2$ from its halide.
options.D: Incorrect because it leaves out 1. Oxidation numbers clearly change, with electron transfer from $Br^-$ to $Cl_2$, so redox must be included.
